Subject: Time-boxed evaluation - pricing & extension request

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the KV caching demo. We're in the middle of our 3-week evaluation but are hitting a couple of integration snags (SAML + network egress rules) that will push our validation timeline out.

Two quick asks:
- Can Brightline get an additional 2-week extension on the time-boxed evaluation? We won't need new seats, just a longer window to finish the end-to-end QA.
- If we do extend, are you open to a small pilot discount (one-time credit or % off) for the extended period? Procurement typically wants some signal of partnership before I push a pilot to them.

We have internal budget discussions next Tuesday — if you can outline options (extension only vs. extension + credit), that would be super helpful. I attached our standard evaluation MOU for reference (Brightline-ma-trial-terms.pdf).

Best,
Sarah Hayes
Senior Product Manager
Brightline Health
[sarah.hayes@brightline.health]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Time-boxed evaluation - pricing & extension request

Sarah —

Appreciate the heads-up and thanks for sharing the MOU. Short answer: yes, we can extend the evaluation and we have two standard ways we handle this depending on commercial intent. Options below (happy to jump on a quick call to walk through):

Option A — No-cost extension (operational only)
- Two additional weeks at no charge.
- Same evaluation limits (concurrency & token caps) apply.
- No invoice/credit, just an extended access window.
- Best when the customer needs purely extra time to finish integration.

Option B — Extended evaluation + pilot credit (recommended for procurement optics)
- Two-week extension plus a one-time 15% credit applied to usage incurred during the extension (applies to hosted API usage only).
- Credit visible on the invoice as a line item; requires a short pilot acceptance form (1 page) and PO or confirmation email from procurement.
- For larger commitments (pilot expected to convert to a paid deployment > $X/month), we can consider up to 25% credit but that needs sales leadership sign-off.

If you want the 25% option we need to document a renewal signal (expected deployment size and a two-month conversion target) so I can loop in Marissa for approval. Otherwise, I can provision the two-week no-cost extension today.

I've CC'd Marissa and Vivek to make approval and invoicing seamless if you pick Option B. Also linking our HubSpot deal for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — Jordan flagged this to me. Good morning.

Quick clarifications on our side on discounts for pilot extensions:
- Standard pilot credit: 15% one-time credit (applies to billed hosted API usage during the extension). This is our typical commercial treatment for short time-boxed pilots.
- Escalation for 25%: We can approve up to 25% only when there's a documented conversion path (expected monthly spend post-pilot) and an internal renewal cadence (PO or business owner confirmation). We need the deal economics and a sketch of post-pilot target to approve at that level.

Operational next steps if you want the 15% credit:
1) Jordan will provision a two-week extension on your eval access.
2) Sarah or procurement sends a confirmation email or PO referencing the HubSpot deal id DL-2026-BHL-17.
3) Vivek will issue the credit on the billing invoice for the extension period.

I've attached the pilot pricing grid we use for reference (pilot-pricing-grid.xlsx) — shows thresholds and the typical conversion tiers. If you think you'll need the larger credit, share a short summary of the expected deployment size and target conversion month so I can escalate for a one-off concession.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if that's easier.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0123
